paragraphs.en: From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals’. That’s why there has been such a strong demand for rules that would prevent broadband providers from picking winners and losers online, preserving the freedom and innovation that have been the lifeblood of the Internet.
paragraphs.zh: 从宽带出现之初，消费者权益倡导者和互联网企业就担心，出售宽带连接服务的有线电视公司和电话公司既有能力，也有动机优待关联网站，使其胜过竞争对手的网站。正因如此，人们才如此强烈地要求制定规则，阻止宽带服务商左右网络竞争的输赢，以维护一直作为互联网命脉的自由与创新。

paragraphs.en: Yet that demand has been almost impossible to fill—in part because of pushback from broadband providers, anti-regulatory conservatives and the courts. A federal appeals court weighed in again Tuesday, but instead of providing a badly needed resolution, it only prolonged the fight. At issue before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit was the latest take of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on net neutrality, adopted on a party-line vote in 2017. The Republican-penned order not only eliminated the strict net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission’s authority to require broadband providers to do much of anything. The order also declared that state and local governments couldn’t regulate broadband providers either.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这一诉求几乎无法得到满足，部分原因在于宽带服务商、反对监管的保守派以及法院的抵制。一家联邦上诉法院周二再次介入，却没有给出迫切需要的解决方案，而只是延长了这场争斗。摆在美国哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院面前的争议，是联邦通信委员会（FCC）2017年通过按党派立场投票所采纳的网络中立性最新政策。由共和党人起草的这项命令，不仅取消了该委员会在2015年民主党占多数时通过的严格网络中立性规则，还否认了委员会有权要求宽带服务商采取几乎任何行动。这项命令还宣布，州政府和地方政府也不得监管宽带服务商。

paragraphs.en: The commission argued that other agencies would protect against anti-competitive behavior, such as a broadband-providing conglomerate like AT&T favoring its own video-streaming service at the expense of Netflix and Apple TV.Yet the FCC also ended the investigations of broadband providers that imposed data caps on their rivals’ streaming services but not their own.
paragraphs.zh: 该委员会认为，其他机构会防范反竞争行为，例如美国电话电报公司（AT&T）这样的宽带服务巨头通过损害奈飞和苹果电视的利益，优待自家的流媒体视频服务。然而，联邦通信委员会同时也终止了对一些宽带服务商的调查：这些服务商对竞争对手的流媒体服务设置流量上限，却不对自家服务施加限制。

paragraphs.en: On Tuesday, the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order deregulating broadband providers, citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move.But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that “the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service,” and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to “ avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism.”
paragraphs.zh: 周二，上诉法院援引最高法院2005年一项支持类似放松监管举措的裁决，一致维持了2017年放松宽带服务商监管的命令。但帕特里夏·米利特法官在一份赞同判决结果的意见中有理有据地指出，“这一结果脱离了现代宽带服务的现实”，并表示国会或最高法院可以介入，以“避免使互联网监管困在技术时代错位的局面之中”。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime, the court threw out the FCC’s attempt to block all state rules on net neutrality, while preserving the commission’s power to preempt individual state laws that undermine its order. That means more battles like the one now going on between the Justice Department and California, which enacted a tough net neutrality law in the wake of the FCC’s abdication.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，法院否决了联邦通信委员会阻止各州制定任何网络中立性规则的企图，同时保留了该委员会排除个别有损其命令的州法律适用的权力。这意味着，类似目前司法部与加利福尼亚州之间的争端会越来越多；在联邦通信委员会放弃监管职责之后，加州颁布了一部严格的网络中立性法律。

paragraphs.en: The endless legal battles and back-and-forth at the FCC cry out for Congress to act. It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on their network and to create clear rules protecting openness and innovation online.
paragraphs.zh: 无休止的法律争斗以及联邦通信委员会政策的反复，迫切要求国会采取行动。国会需要一劳永逸地明确授权该委员会，禁止宽带服务商干预其网络上的流量，并制定清晰规则，保护网络的开放与创新。
